hints: Notice the oil drop is held stationary, so its weight $mg$ downwards must be exactly balanced by the upward electric force $qE$.
Recall the uniform field between the plates is set by the given $V$ and $d$ as $E = V/d$.
Set $mg = qE = qV/d$ and rearrange to isolate $q/m$ before comparing with the four expressions.
walkthrough: Stationary means resultant force is zero, so upward electric force equals downward weight: $qE = mg$.
For parallel plates the uniform electric field strength is $E = V/d$, where $V$ is in volts and $d$ is in $\text{m}$.
Check units: $g$ in $\text{m s}^{-2}$ times $d$ in $\text{m}$ divided by $V$ in $\text{V}$ gives $\text{C kg}^{-1}$ as required.

options.A: Balances $mg = qV/d$ to give $q/m = gd/V$, which matches the force equilibrium.
options.B: Inverts the correct ratio, giving $V/dg$ instead of $dg/V$ from $mg = qV/d$.
options.C: Gives $gV/d$ which has wrong arrangement of $V$ and $d$ and does not satisfy $mg = qE$.
options.D: Gives $d/Vg$ which is the reciprocal of the correct expression and has incorrect units.
